keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the first Piedmontese Republic, 1798 to 20 June 1799 ('declared on 10 September 1798 ... conquered by Austro-Russian troops'). The page gives no area or boundary; Piedmont and Aosta are my reading of 'the territory of Piedmont'. Cliopatria draws these years inside its Kingdom of Sardinia (shape 1797: 55,532 km2).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the re-established republic, 20 June 1800 to 11 September 1802, 'a short-lived republic that existed between 1800 and 1802 on the territory of Piedmont'. The page gives no area (the gazetteer's Piedmont and Aosta come to about 32,000 km2). After Lunéville (March 1801) French control was complete.

ledger.note: December 1798: the French occupy Turin and the Piedmontese Republic replaces the king's mainland rule. Charles Emmanuel IV page: 'On 6 December 1798 the French, under Joubert, occupied Turin and forced Charles Emanuel to abdicate all his territories'. The Subalpine Republic page says the republic 'was declared on 10 September 1798', which conflicts with this and with the kingdom-of-sardinia dossier (French occupation December 1798); the December date is kept. [Reviewer eu-20-x, 2026-11-01: month changed from 9 to 12 and source from the Subalpine Republic page to the Charles Emmanuel IV page.]

ledger.note: 20 June 1799: Austro-Russian troops end the Piedmontese Republic. The republic existed until 'when it was conquered by Austro-Russian troops'; the page dates the end to 20 June 1799 and names no Austrian administration.

ledger.note: 20 June 1800: Napoleon re-establishes the republic. 'The Piedmontese Republic was re-established on 20 June 1800'; the local government was the 'Piedmontese Nation', with a Commission of Government from 27 June to 24 December 1800. The page gives no Austrian withdrawal date.

ledger.note: 11 September 1802: Piedmont and Aosta become French departements. 'The Subalpine Republic ceased to exist on 11 September 1802, when it was divided between the French Republic and the Italian Republic'; France annexed 'Doire, Marengo' and the départements of Pô, Sesia, Stura and Tanaro.

ledger.note: 11 September 1802: the Subalpine Republic ends. Charles Emmanuel IV had abdicated on 4 June 1802 in favour of Victor Emmanuel I; the republic is divided between France (six departements) and the Italian Republic (Agogna).

wars.outcome: Austro-Russian troops conquered the Piedmontese Republic on 20 June 1799; Napoleon returned to Italy in 1800 and the republic was re-established on 20 June 1800 ('Napoleon returned to Italy, taking back much of the new republics').

notes: New dossier, a state Cliopatria lacks; the Piedmont years 1797-1813 are drawn inside Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sardinia (kingdom-of-sardinia, whose ledger carries them as French and Austrian occupations 1798-1802: the occupation events there pair with the loss/gain here). One page only (the budget for a minor state); it gives no area, no boundary and no Marengo date. The page's 10 September 1798 date for the declaration conflicts with other readings: the Sardinia dossier has the king leaving Turin on 6 December 1798 and France occupying Piedmont in December 1798; the dossier keeps the page's date at confidence 2 and a reviewer should check it against the Piedmontese Republic or Charles Emmanuel IV pages. The page treats the 1798-99 Piedmontese Republic and the 1800-02 Subalpine Republic as one entity ('re-established'); the year between (June 1799-June 1800) is Austro-Russian rule. The Treaty of Luneville (March 1801, French control complete as 'Subalpine Gaul') changes the republic's status but has no ledger type for it. Aosta resolves through the gazetteer as 'Aosta'.
